hero.subheadline: The world has the chips, but it lacks the 'plumbing'—the power and cooling needed to run them. We are building the plumbing in Kenya.

sections.title: The Invisible Bottleneck in AI Growth
sections.body: Mainstream media often focuses on the shortage of NVIDIA chips, but a more permanent and structural shortage is emerging: the shortage of high-density data center capacity. Standard data centers, built for web hosting and enterprise database storage, are not equipped to handle the 40kW-100kW per rack power requirements of modern AI clusters. Major tech hubs like Northern Virginia, Dublin, and Singapore have reached the limits of their electrical grids, leading to a freeze on new data center permits. This 'Gridlock' is our greatest opportunity. Kenya AI Compute circumvents the supply crisis by building vertically integrated capacity where power is abundant and industrial space is ready. We are providing the 'Critical Compute Real Estate' that the world's AI models are desperately searching for. sections.title: The Supply Crisis Factors
items: Grid Saturation: Traditional tech capitals can no longer support high-density power growth.
Legacy Infrastructure: 80% of existing data centers cannot support modern GPU cooling needs.
Permit Delays: New facility construction in the West now takes 3-5 years due to regulation.
Power Costs: High electricity prices in Europe make AI training economically unsustainable.
Geographic Concentration: 90% of compute is in 3 regions; the world needs localized diversity.
